title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pages 650 bis–787 continuing the Longue Marche notes). Grothendieck is building, over a base S, a group scheme G_{ρ,σ} generated by two elements ρ (order-3 type) and σ (order-2/4 type), acting on a rank-2 lattice M = Zλ0 ⊕ Zλ1 and its vector-group version M̲ = M⊗G_a. He computes the subgroup scheme Z_{ρ,σ}, a centraliser- or stabiliser-like object, through an auxiliary functor Σ^{ff}_{ρ,σ} of systems (μ̲; ξ0, η0). Here μ̲ lies in a torus-like group scheme O*_12 (D*_12). Judging by the name, this is probably the unit group of a cyclotomic order of level 12 viewed as a scheme, but that is my reading. On the previous page: M0 = Zδ ⊕ Z(3λ1), with δ = λ1−λ0 and 3λ1 = (1−ρ)δ, and Σ^{ff} ≅ D*_12 × Zδ.

On this page:
- (140) When 2 is invertible, Σ^{ff}(S) embeds into (M̲0 × {0,1} × {0,1})(S) by (μ̲; ξ0, η0) ↦ (ξ0, ε2(μ̲), ε3(μ̲)). The ε_i are discrete sign or parity invariants of μ̲, written ν2, ν3 ∈ {0,1}.
- The image is described by writing ξ0 = η0·δ + ν''·(3λ1), with η0, ν'' ∈ Γ(S, G_a), and imposing (141):
  - ν''+ν2−ν3(+2ν2ν3) is divisible by 2, which is automatic once 2 is invertible;
  - (−5)^{ν2}·5^{ν3} + 6(ν''+ν2−ν3+2ν2ν3) is a unit. He simplifies this to 1 − 2ν3 − 2ν2ν3 + 6ν''.
- So Σ^{ff} is open in a rank-2 vector group times a finite constant scheme. Hence Σ^{ff}, and with it Z_{ρ,σ}, is smooth of relative dimension 2.
- (142) gives the extension 1 → Z^{+0}_{ρ,σ} → Z_{ρ,σ} → O'_12 → 1. Here Z^{+0} ≅ G_a ≅ Zδ ⊗ G_a, via λ ↦ (μ̲=1, ξ0=λδ, η0=λδ).
- (143) defines the line L0 = {λ·λ0 : λ ∈ Γ G_a} ⊂ M̲.
- (144) maps L0 → Z_{ρ,σ} by ℓ ↦ (int(ℓ), 1), i.e. inner conjugation by the translation ℓ. On the Σ side this is ℓ ↦ ((1−ρ_M)ℓ, (1−σ_M)ℓ) = (λ0−λδ, −λδ) for ℓ = λλ0.
- The next page draws the consequences: L0 ≅ Z^{+0}, the quotient V = Z/L0 ≅ O*_12, a canonical section, a semidirect-product description, and finally G_{ρ,σ} ≅ O*_12 · 𝔖^+.

Purpose: to exhibit a smooth group-scheme model of the 'ρ,σ' group, as an extension of an O*_12 part by a vector/translation part. This appears to be part of a scheme-theoretic treatment of the modular/Teichmüller group (SL2(Z) as an amalgam of orders 4 and 6) relevant to the Galois–Teichmüller programme.
errors: Possible arithmetic slip in the under-brace of (141). For ν2, ν3 ∈ {0,1} one has (−5)^{ν2} = 1−6ν2 and 5^{ν3} = 1+4ν3. Their product plus 6(ν''+ν2−ν3+2ν2ν3) equals 1 − 2ν3 − 12ν2ν3 + 6ν'', not 1 − 2ν3 − 2ν2ν3 + 6ν''. Either the coefficient is a slip, or the handwriting '2ν2ν3' was misread.

The parenthetical 'λ0 − λδ' in (144) is hard to reconcile with (1−ρ_M)(λλ0), which should be λ-linear (one would expect something like λ(λ0−...)). It may be a shorthand or a transcription problem; I cannot verify it without the definition of ρ_M from earlier pages.

The smoothness claim is justified only over Z[1/2], where the divisibility condition is automatic. The remark 'en tout état de cause' suggests he believes it holds over the whole base, but the argument given on this page covers only the case where 2 is invertible.

ideas.what: Describing a centraliser-type subgroup scheme Z_{ρ,σ} as an open subscheme of a rank-2 vector group times a finite constant scheme, hence smooth of relative dimension 2
ideas.modern_name: smoothness of a stabiliser/centraliser group scheme via an explicit open embedding
ideas.where_published: Technique of SGA 3 type; this specific computation is unpublished

ideas.what: Extension 1 → G_a → Z_{ρ,σ} → O*_12 → 1, then splitting by quotienting by the translation line L0 and finding a canonical section, so that G_{ρ,σ} ≅ O*_12 · 𝔖^+
ideas.modern_name: a group-scheme model (semidirect product of a torus-like unit group with an affine/translation group) for a group generated by elements of order 3 and 2/4
ideas.usually_credited_to: unclear; related to the algebraic or pro-unipotent hulls of SL2(Z) studied in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory (Drinfeld, Ihara, Hain–Matsumoto)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to La Longue Marche (1981), which remains essentially unpublished

ideas.what: Inner automorphisms by translations ℓ ∈ L0 giving the subgroup ℓ ↦ ((1−ρ)ℓ, (1−σ)ℓ)
ideas.modern_name: coboundary map / translation cocycles in an affine group

missed.claim: An explicit scheme-theoretic (over Z[1/2]) model of the ρ,σ-group as O*_12 ⋉ (affine part), with discrete invariants ε2, ε3 and the arithmetic unit condition involving ±5 and 6. It appears to be a fragment of a programme of 'schematising' the modular/Teichmüller groups that has no published counterpart, though the page itself is routine computation.
missed.quote: Σ^{ff}_{ρ,σ} donc aussi Z_{ρ,σ} est lisse de dim relative 2
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It may document a concrete attempt at an integral group-scheme hull of SL2(Z)-type groups, distinct from the pro-unipotent/relative completions later studied by Hain and others. Assessing this needs the surrounding pages.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a detailed but routine structural computation, an open embedding giving smoothness plus an extension analysis, inside an unpublished project. It is interesting only as evidence of the broader schematisation programme; nothing on the page is a striking standalone result.
transcription_corrections: The under-brace reads '1 − 2ν3 − 2ν2ν3 + 6ν''' in the image (with a correction over the first coefficient); arithmetically one would expect −12ν2ν3.
'Γ[?] G_a(S)' should probably read 'Γ G_a(S)' or 'Γ(S, G_a)'.
In (144) the target is Z^{+0}_{ρ,σ} (≅ Σ^{ff,+0}_{ρ,σ}), with the superscript partly struck; the next page confirms L0 ≅ Z^{+0}_{ρ,σ}.
